subject.title: fix(models): add provider request rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw core accept an opt-in `models.providers.*.request.rateLimit` config surface for provider HTTP dispatch now, or keep this work in the canonical rate-limit tracker until the broader API boundary is chosen?
rationale: This PR is not blocked by a clear code defect; the unresolved choice is whether this new public config and local queue/rejection behavior is the product shape maintainers want to support.

options.title: Close Until Sponsored
options.body: Close this PR as technically useful but product-unconfirmed, and invite a maintainer-sponsored replacement or reopen once the config/API direction is approved.

options.title: Sponsor Provider Dispatch First
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly approve this narrow provider-dispatch config surface, then require a rebase and final review before merge.

options.title: Fold Into Canonical Design
options.body: Keep rate limiting under the broader tracker and design one policy surface that also covers budgets, status, persistence, and non-provider calls.

recommendation.title: Close Until Sponsored
recommendation.body: Close this PR as technically useful but product-unconfirmed, and invite a maintainer-sponsored replacement or reopen once the config/API direction is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent signal on adjacent provider egress boundaries and are the best available owner for deciding whether this public config surface belongs in core now.
